e2e.Name: Idea-to-Business Plan
e2e.Goal: Evaluate the initial opportunity, identify the target market, and produce a preliminary business plan.

e2e.Name: Idea-to-Business Proposal
e2e.Goal: Conduct the opportunity study, develop a detailed business case, and take the Go/No-Go decision.

e2e.Name: Business Proposal-to-Design
e2e.Goal: Complete the detailed design and functional prototype, and validate the architecture.

e2e.Name: Design-to-Development
e2e.Goal: Complete development, validate functionalities, and prepare deployment.

e2e.Name: Development-to-Launch
e2e.Goal: Prepare and execute the market launch.

e2e.Name: Launch-to-After-Sales
e2e.Goal: Monitor post-launch performance, analyze feedback, and track incidents.

e2e.Name: After-Sales-to-Performance
e2e.Goal: Evaluate overall performance and profitability, and prepare the relaunch-or-retire decision.

e2e.Name: Assessment-to-Relaunch or Retirement
e2e.Goal: Branching decision: relaunch the product (loop back to E2E-03/04/05) or retire it (proceed to T6).

e2e.Name: Market Strategy-to-Campaign
e2e.Goal: Establish the market strategy and execute marketing campaigns.

E2E-01.trigger: Market trend detected, strategic initiative launched, or executive request for new product exploration.
E2E-01.terminal: Approved Business Plan with committed resources; Go decision at T-1 to proceed to E2E-02 (Idea-to-Business Proposal).

tasks.name: Capture Strategic Idea
tasks.description: Capture new product/service idea from an internal or external source

tasks.name: Assess Market Opportunity
tasks.description: Analyze market trends, customer needs, and competitive landscape

tasks.name: Build Preliminary Business Case
tasks.description: Develop preliminary business case with NPV, ROI, and risk

tasks.name: Assess Risks & Compliance
tasks.description: Identify regulatory, legal, and technical risks

tasks.name: Describe High-Level Capability
tasks.description: Define high-level product capability and skills needed

tasks.name: Establish Product Portfolio Strategy
tasks.description: Align idea with portfolio strategy and roadmap

tasks.name: Approve T-1 Gate (Go/No-Go)
tasks.description: Gate Review Board decision to proceed

E2E-02.trigger: T-1 Gate Go decision from E2E-01.
E2E-02.terminal: Approved Business Proposal; T0 Gate Go decision to proceed to E2E-03 (Design).

E2E-03.trigger: T0 Gate Go decision from E2E-02.
E2E-03.terminal: Validated design and functional prototype; T1 Gate Go decision to proceed to E2E-04 (Development).

tasks.name: Develop Detailed Specifications
tasks.description: Develop detailed commercial, performance, technical, and operational specifications

E2E-04.trigger: T1 Gate Go decision from E2E-03.
E2E-04.terminal: Completed development and validated functionalities; T2 Gate Go decision to proceed to E2E-05 (Launch).

E2E-05.trigger: T2 Gate Go decision from E2E-04.
E2E-05.terminal: Product launched; T3 Gate Go-Live decision, which opens E2E-06 (After-Sales), E2E-07 (Performance), E2E-08 (Relaunch/Retire) and E2E-09 (Campaign).

E2E-06.trigger: T3 Gate Go decision from E2E-05.
E2E-06.terminal: Post-launch performance monitored; T4 Gate Go decision to proceed to E2E-07 (Performance).

tasks.name: Track Product Performance
tasks.description: Track product performance in the field

E2E-07.trigger: T4 Gate Go decision from E2E-06.
E2E-07.terminal: Overall performance evaluated; T5 Gate decision for Relaunch or Retirement, which triggers E2E-08.

E2E-08.trigger: T5 Gate decision from E2E-07 (Relaunch or Retirement).
E2E-08.terminal: Branch A (Relaunch): product re-enters E2E-03 (Design), E2E-04 (Development), or E2E-05 (Launch). Branch B (Retirement): product retired; T6 Gate End-of-Life confirmed.

E2E-09.trigger: Portfolio strategy approved; runs in parallel with all other E2E processes.
E2E-09.terminal: Marketing campaign executed; effectiveness measured; insights fed back to E2E-01 and E2E-07.

chains.Description: E2E-01 produces the Business Plan that triggers E2E-02 (Opportunity Study).
The T0 Go decision opens Design (E2E-03), Development (E2E-04) and Launch (E2E-05).
The T1 Design decision feeds Development (E2E-04).
The T2 Development decision feeds Launch (E2E-05).
The T3 Go-Live decision opens After-Sales, Performance, Relaunch/Retire and Campaign.
The T4 After-Sales decision feeds the Performance Review (E2E-07).
The T5 Performance decision triggers the E2E-08 branching decision.

chains.Related to: E2E-03, E2E-04, E2E-05 (Branch A) or terminal (Branch B)
chains.Description: Branch A loops back to E2E-03, 04 or 05; Branch B retires the product at T6.
Runs in parallel to supply market strategy and campaigns to all other processes.

trackRules.title: Light Track performance review without T4
trackRules.text: In the Light Track, E2E-07 starts after the T3 Go-Live decision plus an observation period set by the Innovation Governance Board (for example, two quarters). UFT-06-04 (Track Customer Satisfaction) and UFT-06-05 (Track Product Performance) run in light form during that period.

trackRules.title: Fast Track tasks that depend on non-activated macro processes
trackRules.text: Nine user-facing tasks (UFT-01-02, UFT-01-04, UFT-02-04, UFT-02-06, UFT-05-03, UFT-05-04, UFT-05-05, UFT-05-07, UFT-05-08) rely on MP-17, MP-30 or MP-32, which are not activated in the Fast Track. They are marked skippable in the Fast Track configuration; MP-30 becomes mandatory when the change affects a regulated product.

trackRules.title: Fast Track has no performance or retirement path
trackRules.text: Every Fast Track project is a change to an existing product. After T3, its performance and eventual retirement are governed by the parent product lifecycle (its own E2E-07 and E2E-08).

trackRules.title: Light Track macro process count
trackRules.text: The Light Track mandates 21 macro processes; the 40 to 50 range assumes 19 to 29 optional macro processes are selected per project. Recommended optional sets per project type are published as reusable templates (for example, "regional variant" adds MP-30, MP-39, MP-22).

gates.Decision question: Is the idea strategically aligned and worth a funded opportunity study?
gates.Minimum evidence: Captured idea; market opportunity assessment; preliminary business case (NPV, ROI, risk); initial risk and compliance register; portfolio fit.

gates.Decision question: Should we commit investment to design and development?
gates.Minimum evidence: Opportunity study; detailed business case and profitability analysis; high-level functional specifications; preliminary customer journey; regulatory validation; technical feasibility; development plan.

gates.Decision question: Is the design validated and ready to be built?
gates.Minimum evidence: Detailed specifications; validated marketing specifications and customer journey; process models; detailed design; functional prototype; architecture validation; detailed development plan.

gates.Decision question: Is the product complete, tested and operationally ready?
gates.Minimum evidence: Completed functionalities; operational readiness and acceptance test results; configuration baseline; offering procedures; preliminary launch plan.

gates.Decision question: Are we ready to go live?
gates.Minimum evidence: Detailed launch and communication plans; marketing and sales materials; trained teams; validated customer journey; final regulatory validation.

gates.Decision question: Is post-launch performance stable enough for steady-state review?
gates.Minimum evidence: Issue log; performance assessment; campaign results; CSAT and NPS; field performance data.

gates.Decision question: Should the product continue, be relaunched, or be retired?
gates.Minimum evidence: Overall performance evaluation; profitability analysis; customer experience feedback; improvement recommendations.

gates.Decision question: Is the product fully and compliantly retired?
gates.Minimum evidence: Exit impact assessment; exit strategy; executed market exit; end-of-life communication; customer migration; financial closure.

gateOutcomes.text: The project proceeds; the next E2E process starts.
The project stops; resources are released and lessons learned are recorded.
The project pauses, for example pending a market or regulatory event; a re-review date is set.
The project returns to named earlier tasks to close evidence gaps, then comes back to the same gate.

gateRoles: In every E2E process, the checklist task is performed by Quality Assurance (R) and owned by the Product Manager (A); the gate decision is performed by the Executive Sponsor (R) and owned by the Gate Review Board (A). Contentious decisions are escalated under MP-121 (task 13), and exceptions or waivers are recorded under MP-121 (task 15) and MP-122 (task 13).
